note: Prohibition-and-prescription pairs, the shape a brand notebook actually holds. Each topic appears twice, once as a rule about what to do and once about what never to do, so topical similarity alone cannot separate them and only polarity can. Hand-written, so it measures the judgement of whoever wrote it.

passages.name-do: Call the people who buy from us customers. It is the word they use for themselves and the word we use in every channel.
passages.name-dont: Never call the people who buy from us clients. Clients is agency language and it reads as distant and transactional.
passages.price-do: Quote the monthly figure first and the annual saving second. Lead with 79 dollars a month, then note that paying yearly takes two months off.
passages.price-dont: Do not quote a discounted price without the date the discount ends. An open-ended sale figure makes the list price look dishonest.
passages.claims-do: Back every performance claim with the measurement behind it, in the same sentence, with the period it covers.
passages.claims-dont: Avoid superlatives in performance claims. Best, fastest and leading are forbidden unless a cited number sits beside them.
passages.tone-do: Write plainly and in short sentences. Say what the product does and let the reader decide what it is worth.
passages.tone-dont: Never write in the second person plural about feelings. We know how you feel is the exact register this brand refuses.
passages.comp-do: Name a competitor only when comparing a specific, published, verifiable figure, and link the source.
passages.comp-dont: Do not characterise a competitor's intentions or finances. Stick to what their own published material says.
passages.legal-do: Include the standard efficacy footnote on any page that mentions clinical outcomes.
passages.legal-dont: Never state or imply a medical outcome on a product page. Outcomes belong in the evidence section with the footnote.
passages.chan-do: Post long-form thinking to the blog and let social carry a single line and a link.
passages.chan-dont: Do not reproduce a full blog post inside a social caption. Split attention across two surfaces loses both.
